lane: intensity lane (presence-only point process + 1 km zoning + break-even tiling)
hypothesis: A presence-only Poisson point-process intensity fitted on the published fault catalogue, with mapping-effort channels as covariates, ranks 1 km blocks by EXPECTED NEW-FAULT TRACE DENSITY; tiling only the blocks whose predicted density clears the break-even bar implied by the organizer's own alpha=0.2 term beats tiling every block, because a lattice only pays above ~1-2% density.
mechanism: DTI = TP_w/(0.2*TP_w + 0.2*FP_w + 0.8*|G|), so d(DTI)/d(mass at x) = (Delta(x)*D_ - 0.2*A)/D_^2 and a pixel pays iff Delta(x) >= 0.2*DTI. At the group's incumbent 0.2778 that bar is 0.0556; for a 10x10 px block it is 100*0.2*DTI/3 = 1.85 trace px per block.
named_non_fault_process_that_could_mimic: Drainage networks and alluvial-fan distributary channels. They are linear, they are continuous at 1-10 km, they concentrate where relief and lithology contrast are highest - which is also where the lidar scarp channels (l_ex_max, l_step_max, l_relief, ridge_det_elev) fire. The single-channel screen is consistent with this: the strongest in-model channel is trace_density (AUC 0.5801 on the canary fold), and the top 4 channels are either catalogue-derived (leakage) or trace_density. A raster built on these channels could be ranking drainage, not faults, and the holdout cannot distinguish the two because the withheld positives are also catalogue faults.

holdout.design: hide-and-recover: whole 8-connected catalogue components withheld + 2 px buffer; every catalogue-derived channel refitted from visible faults only; withheld pixels masked pixel-exactly
holdout.ci_note: n=2 folds only. The t-interval with 1 degree of freedom is +/-0.0121 and is not a meaningful confidence interval; the honest summary is the RANGE [0.0872, 0.0891]. More folds are queued work, not done.
holdout.note: HOLDOUT-DTI on the published catalogue. NOT a competition score and NOT comparable to the leaderboard.

uniqueness.dots_verdict: NO DRIFT - unique against all 696 registered rasters
uniqueness.dots_verdict_basis: max chance-corrected lift 1.999, and that is on a 244-dot registry raster with raw overlap 0.0012. The literal >0.70 rule is tripped by 20 of 696 rasters, but those are dense continuous surfaces: the maximum lift among them is 1.068 (272,853-dot raster covering 69.6% of the footprint within 3 px) and several have lift exactly 1.000 because they are positive over all 5,167,373 footprint pixels, so any dot pattern trips the literal rule against them.

submission_note: 1 km new-fault-density zoning then break-even tiling: 38,593 dots, min sep 3.16 px, 0 within 200 m of the mapped catalogue. UNSCORED.

verdict.meaning: the candidate clears every gate this repository can test offline: format, range, grid contract, uniqueness against all 696 registered rasters, and a leakage-clean holdout. It has NO organizer score. 'promote' means 'ready for the separate selector step', NOT 'known to beat 0.2778'.
